# R386: FP32 gated plane over the shared Prefill region

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source/lifetime audit. No implementation, build, test, import, GPU/device query, process/service operation, Git mutation, or cleanup. This report is the only write.

Candidate source: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-prefill-12k-20261013`, HEAD `499f226a0f3b46aa1bdcd0314fd0f81558799f6f`, with 10 dirty paths as supplied. Qualified comparison source: `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013`, HEAD `7b51af7daaccf47d181f73f24590bd43d97b9b0b`. The registry read was `bench/results/2026-10-13-upstream-benchsh-phase-cache-pair/report-registry-v190.json` in the qualified tree; it records 929 completed research items, names R384 as the gated-plane audit and R385 as the compact-MoE report, and says main alone executes tests. R384's detailed source baseline is the earlier qualified tree at parent 499f226a. This report rechecks the live candidate source seam and relies on no performance inference.

## Conclusion

The gate plane can be overlaid on the existing shared GDN/QSA/MoE region **after** `gr_mix_r` only if the implementation makes the two storage intervals explicit and retains the current ordered compute-queue contract. The source has the right phase boundary: both hyperconnection halves materialize `m.gated`, consume it exactly in `gr_mix_r`, then submit the attention GDN/QSA or FFN MoE work that uses the shared region. There is no source read of `m.gated` after that mix in the normal layer path. GDN/QSA/MoE writers cannot be allowed to begin until the mix has finished; same in-order queue submission gives that dependency today.

This is a promising allocator overlay, not a proven implementation. It requires a coordinated count/carve/relayout change and tests for both HC halves and all active shared-region alternatives. A raw pointer alias at init is safe only if the startup and every actual Prefill reinit use the same in-order compute queue and the gate is not read concurrently with any region writer. Do not infer this result for the separate single-token decode `GrWorkspace`; it still needs its own plane and has a different consumer.

## Exact seam and queue ownership

In `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`, the normal carve takes the FP32 gate plane separately at 826–830, before it takes the shared block region at 846–852. The latter is sized as `max(gdn_set_bytes(T), qsa_set_bytes(...), moe_set_bytes(T,...))`; independent typed GDN, QSA and MoE views are then carved from the same base at 853–900. `Prefill::bytes_needed` repeats the separate gate take and max-region take at 1134–1148. The corresponding owned allocation order is reproduced in `carve`; borrowed and relayout paths must be audited against that same ordering, not just `bytes_needed`.

The normal per-layer boundary is at 1735 onward. For each half, `hc_attn_*` or `hc_ffn_*` selects its own norm/down/up/inject weights. The code queues norm, down projection, SiLU, up projection into `m.gated`, injection projection into `m.inj`, then `gr_mix_r` at 1744–1753. `gr_mix_r` reads `R`, row scales, norm weights and every gate element, writes `mixed` and BF16 images, and contains no writes to the gate plane (`src/prefill/kernels.cpp:281 onward)). The next code submits GDN projections/gates/convolution/recurrence/output at 1755 onward or the QSA projections and attention path, all on `m.cs`; after the block work, MoE's FFN-half path consumes the same shared-region allocation before the HC residual write at 3005–3035. The residual write reads `m.inj`, not `m.gated`.

The candidate's ordinary `Prefill` stream is an engine stream. `src/core/device.cpp:197–202,278–282` creates engine streams with `sycl::property::queue::in_order`, including when profiling is enabled. The current 12K scratch-alias admission additionally checks that property in `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:700–707`. The `Gemm` wrapper binds one `stream_` and sends oneMath GEMM or native/XMX kernels to that same queue (`src/prefill/gemm.cpp:317–340)); oneMath GEMM is asynchronous and returns an event in its API, so correctness here comes from the same in-order queue contract, not host completion. SYCL's primary queue reference says in-order commands have implicit dependencies on the prior command on that queue and makes no ordering promise across queues; oneMath's GEMM accepts a queue and optional dependencies. [SYCL queue ordering](https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/queue.html), [oneMath GEMM API](https://oneapi-spec.uxlfoundation.org/specifications/oneapi/v1.4-rev-1/elements/onemath/source/domains/blas/gemm). If this overlay is generalized to an out-of-order queue, add explicit event dependencies from the last gate producer through `gr_mix_r` and from mix completion to the first region writer; a host-side wait is unnecessary on the current in-order stream.

The other queue and thread users do not authorize a writer to race this interval. Expert blob staging uses `m.copy` and separate ring/stage storage; it does not carve the shared region. A CPU expert pool writes separate CPU output storage and copies into `m.Dm` on `m.cs`. PLE's batch helper does use local views carved from `m.region` at 1682–1715, but it is submitted earlier in layer 1 and its postops are on `m.cs`; its temporary variable also named `gated` is PLE's smaller, separate local plane, not `m.gated`. The optional draft KV path has its own gate view carved from `m.region` and ends with an explicit `stream_sync(m.cs)` before return at 1092–1110. It is a serialized consumer of the region and does not extend the normal HC gate lifetime. There is no source evidence of a second compute queue writing `m.region` during the normal gate/mix interval.

## Both halves and readers

The main path loops over `half=0,1` inside each layer, so the same `m.gated` address is used for both independent HC parameter sets. In half 0, it is read by `gr_mix_r` before GDN or QSA uses the shared block region. In half 1, it is read by `gr_mix_r` before the MoE branch uses that region. The attention result is written back to `R` before half 1 starts; the next gate production overwrites the whole T×D gate plane before its own mix. Conversely, do not alias the gate to `R`: `gr_mix_r` must still read R while consuming the gate. Injection stays separate because its last read is the later residual write.

There are two additional gate-producing call sites in `run_draft` (currently around 1087–1093): one attention HC norm/down/up/mix pass per draft batch, then QSA K/V. It carves its own per-batch `gated` view inside `m.region`, not `m.gated`. This path is already region-resident and ends with a compute stream sync. The overlay does not remove that draft-local scratch, and any new helper/refactor should not accidentally redirect it to the full-chunk alias.

## Required count/carve change and source-derived delta

Let `G = align256(T * D * sizeof(float))` be the separate gate take, and `B = max(GDN,QSA,MoE)` be the existing shared take, using the exact same active flags, geometry, batch parameters and Alloc rounding as today. The correct new shared take is `max(G,B)`, with the gate pointer placed at the shared base and every block view still based at that same base but used only after mix. Relative to the present `G+B` takes, the source-requested reduction is exactly `min(G,B)`; it is not automatically the whole G if the active shared region is smaller.

For the stock 12,288-row candidate, `T*D*4 = 12,288*10,240*4 = 503,316,480 B = 480 MiB`; this extent is already 256-byte aligned. R381's source arithmetic for this candidate reports QSA as the current shared-region winner at 1,634,831,104 B (1,559.375 MiB), greater than G. Under that exact geometry/flag set, the proposed overlay therefore saves **503,316,480 requested bytes (480 MiB)** from Prefill's allocation ledger. This is a source-derived count change, not measured physical VRAM freed, fit, speed or performance evidence. Recompute `B` for each current format/flag and relayout configuration; changing compact MoE, MMQ, QSA batch sizes or future geometry may change the winner and therefore the savings. Keep count-only, owned, borrowed and relayout sizing/carving in lockstep.

## Hazards and fixture needed

The key temporal proof is not merely that the gate is lexically dead after `gr_mix_r`: all gate up-projection writes must complete before mix reads, and all block scratch writers must be ordered after the mix's final gate read. The repository's in-order engine queue proves this at submission order for the current implementation. Preserve/revalidate the in-order queue admission in every init/reinit path. If scratch aliasing or another API allows out-of-order streams, reject that mode or wire explicit event dependencies; do not treat different queues as ordered. Error and early-return paths are safe only while the Prefill owner retains the allocation until its existing queue drains; never free/rebind the shared base on a failed asynchronous submission before drain.

The minimal CPU fixture should exercise the sizing equation with synthetic `G<B`, `G=B`, and `G>B`, verify the expected `min(G,B)` delta, 256-byte alignment, overflow rejection, and equality among count-only/owned/borrowed/relayout extents for alias enabled and disabled. A host-only fake allocator can verify pointer identity (gate base equals region base), region-view capacity and unchanged later allocations; it cannot prove device ordering or numerical parity.

The device fixture must use distinctive sentinels/canaries around the shared allocation and compare an unaliased baseline with overlay enabled for (1) attention GDN and QSA layers, (2) FFN MoE, (3) all HC gate/up/inject projections and both residual writes, including the last row and chunk remainder if a non-full T is supported. Compare gate/mixed fingerprints or tensors immediately after mix as well as final layer residual and GDN/QSA/MoE outputs/state. Cover oneMath and the fallback kernel GEMM routes that are actually supported; their queue submission is asynchronous. Include failure/early-return drain cases and an out-of-order queue rejection test. Normal model-level equivalence should preserve existing arithmetic and settings; no gate formula change is proposed here. These are fixture requirements, not executed tests or results.

## Scope exclusions and external references

R384 already rejected moving the up projection past the block and ordinary aliases with `R`, `xn16`, `lo`, or `mixed`; this report does not reopen those candidates. R381's 12K fit/admission work and R356's full-context discussion do not establish physical free-memory headroom for this change. No speedup estimate is made.

Relevant primary implementation sources: candidate `src/prefill/prefill.cpp:826–900, 1015–1110, 1735–1753, 1755 onward, 2981–3035`; `src/prefill/kernels.cpp:281 onward`; `src/prefill/gemm.cpp:288–340`; `src/core/device.cpp:197–202,278–282`. Prior local evidence: R384 `research-hyperconnection-gated-plane-lifetime-round384-v1.txt`, R381 `research-head-alias-12288-admission-round381-v1.txt`, and R376 v2 `research-prefill-total-live-owner-bytes-round376-v2.txt`. No additional tuning recommendation or public developer blog was needed to establish the lifetime contract.
